chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Yaqoob ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Hasan ibn Atiyyah, from Umar ibn Yazid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I heard him say: The gratitude for every blessing, no matter how great, is to praise God, the Mighty and Exalted.
ai.seo_question: What is the primary act of gratitude for all blessings according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the fundamental essence of gratitude (shukr) as praising God (hamd), establishing that recognition of the Giver is the primary response to any blessing, regardless of its size. This aligns with the Shia scholarly emphasis on *shukr al-dawr* (gratitude for the cycle of blessings) and underscores that verbal praise is the foundational act that acknowledges God's sovereignty and generosity. It serves as a practical spiritual discipline, reminding believers that even minor favors warrant explicit acknowledgment of their source.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-73 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted on the authority of Yaqoob ibn Yazid, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Atiye , on the authority of Umar ibn Yazid that he had heard Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) say,
“The gratitude for any blessing - no matter how great it may be - is to praise God the Honorable the Exalted.”
